cards.design_implication: If SSE systematics are not accounted for, PTA GWB searches may yield biased upper limits or false detections; analysis pipelines should incorporate methods to bridge or marginalize over SSE differences.
does_not_establish: The precise mechanism by which SSE errors mimic GWB signals.
The magnitude of bias introduced by any specific SSE model.
cards.evidence_excerpt: For the first time, we find that the GWB constraints are sensitive to the solar system ephemeris (SSE) model used and that SSE errors can mimic a GWB signal.
limitations: The claim is limited to the sensitivity of GWB constraints to SSE models as stated in the abstract.
The specific quantitative impact of unmitigated SSE errors is not detailed in the text.
cards.statement: Pulsar-timing array constraints on the isotropic stochastic gravitational-wave background are sensitive to the solar system ephemeris (SSE) model used, as SSE errors can mimic a GWB signal.

cards.design_implication: Implementing the described SSE-bridging approach is required to achieve robustness against SSE errors in PTA GWB constraints; previous PTA upper limits without this calibration may require revision.
does_not_establish: The exact algorithm or software used to bridge SSE differences.
Whether this method is directly transferable to other PTA collaborations without modification.
cards.evidence_excerpt: We developed an approach that bridges systematic SSE differences, producing the first pulsar-timing array (PTA) constraints that are robust against SSE errors.
limitations: The abstract asserts robustness but does not define the specific mathematical implementation or validation metrics for 'bridging' SSE differences.
The claim is restricted to the context of NANOGrav data analysis for GWB constraints.
cards.statement: A new approach was developed to bridge systematic SSE differences, producing PTA constraints that are robust against SSE errors.

cards.design_implication: Reanalysis of historical PTA data should prioritize quantifying and removing SSE systematics to avoid biased astrophysical interpretations; conclusions drawn from prior SSE-non-marginalized limits should be treated with caution.
does_not_establish: The specific new bounds for every previous study.
The extent to which non-GWB PTA results are affected by SSE systematics.
cards.evidence_excerpt: Previous PTA upper limits on the GWB (as well as their astrophysical and cosmological interpretations) will need revision in light of SSE systematic errors.
limitations: This is a recommendation based on the finding that SSE errors can mimic signals; it does not provide the revised numerical values for all previous limits.
The scope is limited to PTA GWB upper limits and their direct interpretations.
cards.statement: Previous PTA upper limits on the GWB and their astrophysical and cosmological interpretations need revision in light of SSE systematic errors.

cards.design_implication: When designing future searches, sensitivity targets should be benchmarked against this SSE-marginalized limit; detection efforts must aim to improve upon the ~2x factor improvement over nine-year limits.
does_not_establish: Constraints on arbitrary spectral indices or non-power-law models.
A detection of the stochastic background (no evidence was found).
cards.evidence_excerpt: We thus place a 95% upper limit on the GW-strain amplitude of A GWB < 1.45 × 10−15 at a frequency of f = 1 yr−1 for a fiducial f −2/3 power-law spectrum and with interpulsar correlations modeled.
limitations: This limit applies specifically to the fiducial f^-2/3 power-law spectrum.
The limit is derived from NANOGrav 11-year data and is contingent on the specific SSE marginalization approach described.
cards.statement: The 95% upper limit on the GW-strain amplitude for a fiducial f^-2/3 power-law spectrum is constrained to be less than 1.45 × 10^-15 at f = 1 yr^-1 using SSE-robust methods.
